findings.summary: The Decided paragraph says the ship carries on to its next sortie if one is waiting (E4's P4), but the pass always flies to the ship's rest (`goalOf`) and ignores the P4 `waitS`, so a captain with back-to-back summons flies home, sits idle about 1.1 s, then flies out again: the stop-and-go the item set out to remove. This also contradicts 05 P-5 ('a captain never flies home between').
findings.why: movers.ts:317 flies to goalOf (the rest), waitS ignored (movers.ts:253-254); Decided says next sortie; 05 P-5 says never flies home between.

findings.summary: The acceptance check 'the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip' can't fail: it compares two delayMs values from the same act-phase array, and the `actAt` term cancels out. It never ties the blip to when the ship actually reaches the spot.
findings.why: summonPass.test.ts:72 compares two delayMs with actAt cancelling, so it cannot fail.

findings.summary: The solar-dense change sorts captains' turns by whether they moved (12 px or more), so 'parked while named' is now true by definition: a regular sortie that drifts while named gets reclassified as a 'ride' and passes the looser check.
findings.why: solar-dense.spec.ts:458-466 splits by moved>=12, so 'parked while named' holds by construction; rides not checked as summons.

findings.summary: A summon's plate is now whole for only about 1280 ms (NOTE_MIN_MS less the unfurl), below CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS. The 15 §11 CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS row ('However short the work, the plate is whole at least this long') and crewTimes' JSDoc weren't amended; only the CREW_HOLD_MS row was.
findings.why: maneuvers.ts:83 closeMs=openMs+NOTE_MIN_MS bypasses CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS; 15 row at :1259 unchanged.

findings.summary: The call blip, the summons, is drawn in At-rest blue (HERO_GLOW) as Decided requires, but 15 §2 still lists summons under Hero blue and 13 §6.5 still says 'the summons is in hero blue'. Those palette rows are now out of step.
findings.why: stationJumpIn.ts:55 uses HERO_GLOW; 15:120 and 13:738 still say hero blue.

findings.summary: F2 tips Pulsar over a cliff in the director's levers. With every lever, Pulsar now drops 'light' and plays its non-climax beats at TEMPO_MAX 2× instead of 1.1×, and it runs longer. The golden and a carve-out in the test accept this rather than flag it.
findings.why: director.json diff shows Pulsar levers/tempo/estimate changes; pacingBuilt.test.ts carve-out present.
